title: Understanding Bootstrapping
text: Bootstrapping is a statistical method that involves resampling with replacement from a dataset to estimate the distribution of a statistic. It is particularly useful when the theoretical distribution of a statistic is complex or unknown.

title: Sample Size Consideration
text: When using bootstrapping, the sample size of the resamples is typically the same as the original sample size. In this case, you would resample $$500$$ trips from the May $$1$$ dataset.

title: Variance Estimation
text: The variance of the average duration can be estimated by calculating the variance of the means of the bootstrapped samples. This involves computing the mean duration for each resample and then finding the variance of these means.

title: Bootstrapping Process
text:
To estimate the variance of the average duration using bootstrapping, follow these steps:
$$1$$. Randomly select $$500$$ trips with replacement from the May $$1$$ dataset.
$$2$$. Calculate the mean duration for this resample.
$$3$$. Repeat steps $$1$$ and $$2$$ a large number of times (e.g., $$1000$$ times).
$$4$$. Compute the variance of the means obtained in step $$3$$.
